This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# igrep

igrep is an interactive search tool that runs a fast search engine in the background and allows you to pick results interactively and open the selected match in your text editor.

Supported platforms: macOS, Linux (Windows reportedly supported).

Usage
-----
ig [OPTIONS] <PATTERN|--type-list> [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  <PATTERN>    Regular expression used for searching.
  <PATHS>...   Files or directories to search. Directories are searched recursively.
               If not specified, searching starts from current directory.

Options (high level):
  --hidden                    Search hidden files and directories.
  --editor <EDITOR>           Text editor used to open selected match.
  --context-viewer <VIEWER>   Context viewer position at startup [default: none]
  --custom-command <COMMAND>  Custom command used to open selected match. Must contain {file_name} and {line_number} tokens.
  -g, --glob <GLOB>           Include files/directories matching the given glob.
  -h, --help                  Print help information
  -i, --ignore-case           Searches case insensitively.
  -L, --follow                Follow symbolic links while traversing directories
  -S, --smart-case            Smart case sensitivity behavior
  -t, --type <TYPE>           Only search files matching TYPE
  -T, --type-not <TYPE>       Do not search files matching TYPE
  --theme <THEME>             UI color theme [default: dark]
  --type-list                 Show all supported file types and their corresponding globs.
  -V, --version               Print version information.
  -w, --word-regexp           Only show matches surrounded by word boundaries
  -F, --fixed-strings         Exact matches with no regex

Keybindings
-----------
q, Esc, Ctrl+c      Quit
? / F1              Open/close the keymap popup
Down / j            Select next match
Up / k              Select previous match
Right / l           Select match in next file
Left / h            Select match in previous file
gg / Home           Jump to the first match
Shift-g / End       Jump to the last match
Enter               Open current file
dd / Delete         Filter out selected match
dw                  Filter out all matches in current file
v                   Toggle vertical context viewer
s                   Toggle horizontal context viewer
+ / -               Increase/decrease context viewer size
F5 / /              Open search pattern popup
n / m / c / a       Sorting and navigation shortcuts

Specifying text editor
----------------------
Order of precedence when selecting editor:
  1. --editor option
  2. $IGREP_EDITOR environment variable
  3. $VISUAL environment variable
  4. $EDITOR environment variable

Custom command example:
  --custom-command "vim +{line_number} {file_name}"
  or set via environment: IGREP_CUSTOM_EDITOR="vim +{line_number} {file_name}"

Installation
------------
Prebuilt binaries are available from the project releases.
Package managers:
  - Homebrew: `brew install igrep`
  - Scoop: `scoop install igrep`
  - Pacman (Arch): `pacman -S igrep`
  - Alpine: `apk add igrep`

License
-------
See the LICENSE file in this repository for license information.

import pty, os, subprocess, select

def run_pty(cmd, timeout=3):
    import pty, os, subprocess, select, time
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)
    output = b""
    start = time.time()
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], 0.5)
        if r:
            try:
                data = os.read(master, 4096)
                if not data:
                    break
                output += data
            except OSError:
                break
        if p.poll() is not None:
            # drain
            import time as t
            t.sleep(0.2)
            try:
                while True:
                    r,_,_ = select.select([master], [], 0.2)
                    if not r: break
                    data = os.read(master, 4096)
                    if not data: break
                    output += data
            except: pass
            break
    try:
        p.terminate()
    except: pass
    try: p.wait(timeout=1)
    except: p.kill()
    os.close(master)
    return p.returncode, output

def run_pty_interactive(args, send_keys=None, timeout=4, cwd="/tmp"):
    # send_keys: list of (delay, bytes)

    sends = send_keys or []
    while time.time()-start < timeout:

        while sent_idx < len(sends) and sends[sent_idx][0] <= now:
            _, data = sends[sent_idx]
            try: os.write(master, data)

import os, subprocess, time, select, fcntl, pty

def run_pty_interactive(args, send_keys=None, timeout=4, cwd="/tmp"):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    p = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True, cwd=cwd)
    os.close(slave)
    flags = fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_GETFL)
    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    output = b""
    start = time.time()
    sent_idx=0
    sends = send_keys or []
    while time.time()-start < timeout:
        now = time.time()-start
        while sent_idx < len(sends) and sends[sent_idx][0] <= now:
            _, data = sends[sent_idx]
            try: os.write(master, data)
            except Exception as e: print("write err", e)
            sent_idx+=1
        try:
            data = os.read(master, 8192)
            if data:
                output+=data
        except BlockingIOError:
            pass
        except OSError:
            break
        if p.poll() is not None and sent_idx>=len(sends):
            time.sleep(0.3)
            try:
                while True:
                    try:
                        data=os.read(master, 8192)
                        if not data: break
                        output+=data
                    except BlockingIOError: break
                    except OSError: break
            except: pass
            break
        time.sleep(0.05)
    rc = p.poll()
    if rc is None:
        try: p.terminate()
        except: pass
        try: p.wait(timeout=2)
        except: p.kill()
        rc = p.returncode
    os.close(master)
    return rc, output

def run(args, cwd="/tmp/igtest", timeout=3):
    env=os.environ.copy()
    env["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # set winsize

    # Use TIOCSWINSZ? skip
    p = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=cwd, env=env, close_fds=True)
    os.close(slave)

    fcntl.fcntl(master, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags | os.O_NONBLOCK)
    out=b""

    while time.time()-start < timeout:

            data=os.read(master, 8192)
            if data:
                out+=data
                #print(f"got {len(data)}")

                        if not data: break
                        out+=data
                    except BlockingIOError: break
                    except OSError: break

    rc=p.poll()
    if rc is None:
        p.terminate()
        try: p.wait(timeout=1)

    os.close(master)

        if rc is None:
            p.terminate()
            try: p.wait(timeout=1)
            except: p.kill()
            rc=p.returncode
    os.close(master)
    return rc, out

def get_status(cmd, cwd):

    out=cap(f"s1:{win}")
    status=out.splitlines()[-1] if out.splitlines() else ""

# igrep

igrep is an interactive search tool that runs a fast search engine in the background and allows you to pick results interactively and open the selected match in your text editor.

Supported platforms: macOS, Linux (Windows reportedly supported).

Usage
-----
ig [OPTIONS] <PATTERN|--type-list> [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  <PATTERN>    Regular expression used for searching.
  <PATHS>...   Files or directories to search. Directories are searched recursively.
               If not specified, searching starts from current directory.

Options (high level):
  --hidden                    Search hidden files and directories.
  --editor <EDITOR>           Text editor used to open selected match.
  --context-viewer <VIEWER>   Context viewer position at startup [default: none]
  --custom-command <COMMAND>  Custom command used to open selected match. Must contain {file_name} and {line_number} tokens.

mod ig;
use clap::{Arg, Command, ArgAction};
use anyhow::{Context, Result};

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let m = Command::new("igrep")
        .version("1.3.0")
        .about("Interactive Grep")
        .arg(Arg::new("PATTERN").help("Regular expression used for searching").required(true).conflicts_with("type-list"))
        .arg(Arg::new("PATHS").help("Files or directories to search. Directories are searched recursively. If not specified, searching starts from current directory").num_args(1..))
        .arg(Arg::new("editor").long("editor").value_name("EDITOR").help("Text editor used to open selected match").value_parser(["vim","neovim","nvim","nano","code","vscode","code-insiders","emacs","emacsclient","hx","helix","subl","sublime-text","micro","intellij","goland","pycharm","less","fresh"]).conflicts_with("custom-command"))
        .arg(Arg::new("custom-command").long("custom-command").value_name("CUSTOM_COMMAND").help("Custom command used to open selected match. Must contain {file_name} and {line_number} tokens").env("IGREP_CUSTOM_EDITOR").conflicts_with("editor"))
        .arg(Arg::new("theme").long("theme").value_name("THEME").help("UI color theme").default_value("dark").value_parser(["light","dark"]))
        .arg(Arg::new("ignore-case").short('i').long("ignore-case").help("Searches case insensitively").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))

mod ig;
use clap::{Arg, Command, ArgAction};
use anyhow::{Context, Result, anyhow, bail};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::collections::{HashSet, HashMap};

const EDITORS: &[&str] = &["vim","neovim","nvim","nano","code","vscode","code-insiders","emacs","emacsclient","hx","helix","subl","sublime-text","micro","intellij","goland","pycharm","less","fresh"];

fn main() -> Result<()> {
    let m = Command::new("igrep")
        .version("1.3.0")
        .about("Interactive Grep")
        .arg(Arg::new("PATTERN").help("Regular expression used for searching").required(true).conflicts_with("type-list"))
        .arg(Arg::new("PATHS").help("Files or directories to search. Directories are searched recursively. If not specified, searching starts from current directory").num_args(1..))
        .arg(Arg::new("editor").long("editor").value_name("EDITOR").help("Text editor used to open selected match").value_parser(EDITORS).conflicts_with("custom-command"))
        .arg(Arg::new("custom-command").long("custom-command").value_name("CUSTOM_COMMAND").help("Custom command used to open selected match. Must contain {file_name} and {line_number} tokens").env("IGREP_CUSTOM_EDITOR").conflicts_with("editor"))
        .arg(Arg::new("theme").long("theme").value_name("THEME").help("UI color theme").default_value("dark").value_parser(["light","dark"]))
        .arg(Arg::new("ignore-case").short('i').long("ignore-case").help("Searches case insensitively").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("smart-case").short('S').long("smart-case").help("Searches case insensitively if the pattern is all lowercase. Search case sensitively otherwise").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("hidden").short('.').long("hidden").help("Search hidden files and directories. By default, hidden files and directories are skipped").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("follow").short('L').long("follow").help("Follow symbolic links while traversing directories").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("word-regexp").short('w').long("word-regexp").help("Only show matches surrounded by word boundaries").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("fixed-strings").short('F').long("fixed-strings").help("Exact matches with no regex. Useful when searching for a string full of delimiters").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("multiline").short('U').long("multiline").help("Search with pattern contains newline character ('\\n')").action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
        .arg(Arg::new("glob").short('g').long("glob").value_name("GLOB").help("Include files and directories for searching that match the given glob. Multiple globs may be provided").action(ArgAction::Append))
        .arg(Arg::new("type-list").long("type-list").help("Show all supported file types and their corresponding globs").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).required(true).conflicts_with("PATTERN"))

fn draw_all(out: &mut std::io::Stdout, cols: usize, rows: usize, results: &Vec<FileMatches>, filtered: &HashSet<(String, usize)>, selected: usize, viewer: &ViewerMode, viewer_size: i32, show_keymap: bool, keymap_scroll: usize, show_search: bool, search_input: &str, error_msg: &Option<String>, total_matches: usize, total_files: usize, filtered_count: usize, visible_count: usize) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    use crossterm::{cursor, queue};
    use crossterm::terminal::{Clear, ClearType};
    queue!(out, cursor::MoveTo(0,0))?;
    queue!(out, Clear(ClearType::All))?;
    let status_row = rows.saturating_sub(1);
    let main_rows = rows.saturating_sub(1);
    // Build display lines
    struct DL { text: String }
    let mut dls: Vec<DL> = Vec::new();
    for f in results {
        let mut vis: Vec<(usize,String)> = Vec::new();
        for (ln,line) in &f.matches {
            if filtered.contains(&(f.display_path.clone(), *ln)) {continue;}
            vis.push((*ln,line.clone()));
        }
        if vis.is_empty() {continue;}
        dls.push(DL{text: f.display_path.clone()});
        for (ln,line) in vis {
            dls.push(DL{text: format!(" {}: {}", ln, line)});
        }
    }
    match viewer {
        ViewerMode::None => {
            draw_box(out, 0, 0, cols, main_rows, &dls)?;
        }
        ViewerMode::Vertical => {
            let mut left_w = cols/2;
            if viewer_size>=0 { left_w = (cols/2).saturating_sub(viewer_size as usize); } else { left_w = (cols/2).saturating_add((-viewer_size) as usize); }
            if left_w<10 {left_w=10;} if left_w>cols-10 {left_w=cols-10;}
            let right_w = cols.saturating_sub(left_w);
            draw_box(out, 0, 0, left_w, main_rows, &dls)?;
            // viewer content: file content of selected
            let vis = get_visible(results, filtered);
            let mut viewer_lines: Vec<DL> = Vec::new();
            if !vis.is_empty() {
                let (f,_,_) = &vis[selected.min(vis.len().saturating_sub(1))];
                if let Some(fr) = results.iter().find(|r| r.display_path==*f) {
                    if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(&fr.path) {
                        for line in content.lines() {
                            viewer_lines.push(DL{text: line.to_string()});
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            draw_box(out, left_w, 0, right_w, main_rows, &viewer_lines)?;
        }
        ViewerMode::Horizontal => {
            let mut top_h = main_rows/2;
            if viewer_size>=0 { top_h = (main_rows/2).saturating_sub(viewer_size as usize/2); } else { top_h = (main_rows/2).saturating_add((-viewer_size) as usize/2); }
            if top_h<3 {top_h=3;} if top_h>main_rows-3 {top_h=main_rows-3;}
            let bottom_h = main_rows.saturating_sub(top_h);
            draw_box(out, 0, 0, cols, top_h, &dls)?;
            let vis = get_visible(results, filtered);
            let mut viewer_lines: Vec<DL> = Vec::new();
            if !vis.is_empty() {
                let (f,_,_) = &vis[selected.min(vis.len().saturating_sub(1))];
                if let Some(fr) = results.iter().find(|r| r.display_path==*f) {
                    if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(&fr.path) {
                        for line in content.lines() {
                            viewer_lines.push(DL{text: line.to_string()});
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            draw_box(out, 0, top_h, cols, bottom_h, &viewer_lines)?;
        }
    }
    draw_status_line(out, cols, status_row, error_msg, total_matches, total_files, filtered_count, visible_count, selected)?;
    if show_keymap {
        draw_keymap(out, cols, rows, keymap_scroll)?;
    }
    if show_search {
        draw_search(out, cols, rows, search_input)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn validate_custom_command(cmd: &str) -> Result<()> {
    // must contain space
    if !cmd.contains(' ') {
        bail!("Expected program and its arguments");
    }
    let idx = cmd.find(' ').unwrap();
    let args_part = &cmd[idx+1..];
    let file_count = args_part.matches("{file_name}").count();
    if file_count != 1 {
        bail!("Expected one occurrence of '{{file_name}}'.");
    }
    let line_count = args_part.matches("{line_number}").count();
    if line_count != 1 {
        bail!("Expected one occurrence of '{{line_number}}'.");
    }
    Ok(())
}
